Lab 1 - Basic commads in Cisco Packet Tracer
Project Description:
Laboratory 1 introduces students to Cisco Packet Tracer and the basic CLI steps used to set up routers and switches. The lab focuses on understanding the workspace and performing simple device configuration.
Objectives
• Learn the Packet Tracer interface: add devices, place them on the workspace, and connect them with cables.
• Open the CLI and move between User mode and Privileged mode.
• Practice key commands:
enable, configure terminal, hostname, banner motd, exit, end.
• Do basic setup: set a hostname, add simple passwords, save the configuration, and test connectivity with ping.
Skills Gained
• Navigating Packet Tracer
• Using essential CLI commands
• Understanding device modes
• Applying minimal initial configuration and security
Audience
Beginners and students who want a simple introduction to configuring Cisco devices in a simulation environment.

Name: Lab 2 – Static Routes: Basic Connectivity
Project Description:
Laboratory 2 – Static Routing (Short Version)

This lab teaches how to connect different networks in Cisco Packet Tracer using static routes.
What you will learn:

• What static routing is and how it works.

• How to use ip route to tell routers exactly where to send traffic.

• How to test connections with ping and traceroute.

• How to fix routing problems caused by wrong settings.

• How to link multiple subnets so they can communicate.
After the lab you can:

• Explain when static routing is useful.

• Add and check static routes on Cisco routers.

• Solve simple routing and connectivity issues.

• Build small network topologies where all devices can reach each other.
Who it's for:

Beginners and students who want practical experience with basic IP routing in Packet Tracer.

Name: Lab 3 - Static Routing Configuration and End-to-End Connectivity Setup
Project Description:
Laboratory 3 – Advanced Network Setup (Short Version)

This lab gives practical experience building more complex networks in Cisco Packet Tracer.
What you will learn:

• How to configure routers and switches, including interfaces, VLANs, and inter-VLAN routing.

• How to use static routing together with other routing methods.

• How to check and troubleshoot the network with ping, traceroute, and show commands.

• How to add basic security: passwords, access rules, and saving configurations.

• How to build a multi-layer network that looks more like a real setup.
After the lab you can:

• Configure advanced settings on Cisco devices.

• Make different network segments communicate correctly.

• Find and fix routing and configuration problems.

• Use good practices for network structure and security.
Who it's for:

Students and beginners/intermediate learners who want hands-on experience with more realistic network designs.
